cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Hope with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Draw another route for our parade with me. Two streets said no; the town hasn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only route left goes behind the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then take the other pencil. Can you picture people cheering by the loading bay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dad would come. He works there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on the map. Where would a second person stand?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 rank prefixes do not materially change the collaborative invitation; A5 map instruction gives some control, but approval is not the sustained hope-building tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 last route behind supermarket prompts A3 imagined loading-bay cheers; B4 dad attendance prompts A5 second spectator.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies a real remaining constraint and B4 contributes a plausible small supporter, making hope shared rather than imposed by A alone.

heightening.evidence: B4 one possible spectator becomes A5 invitation to imagine a second, a modest earned heightening.

specificity.evidence: A1 parade rejections and B2 route establish thin evidence; B4 workplace explains why Dad might come.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 second person is specific and gentle, while generic hierarchy text adds stiffness.
